independent_unit: one complete time-resolved pass (n = 22 passes); adjacent time samples are NOT independent replicates and are never pooled; the 22 per-pass numbers are the replicates in every blocked test

item1_binned_amplitude_profile.bin_choice: PRIMARY: 8 symmetric bins of |relative_time_min| with 5-min width over [0,40] min (edges 0,5,...,40) - 5 min = 5 nominal samples per pass, so every pass contributes >= 1 sample to nearly every bin, and the bin count stays small relative to n = 22 passes. SECONDARY: 20 fine 2-min bins over [0,40] for the envelope fits (item 5) and a signed 16 x 5-min profile over [-40,40] to expose any left/right asymmetry.

primary_5min_abs_bins.aggregation: per-pass RMS inside the bin (the pass is one observation), then mean of those per-pass numbers across passes; empty bins are skipped

fine_2min_abs_bins.aggregation: per-pass RMS inside the bin (the pass is one observation), then mean of those per-pass numbers across passes; empty bins are skipped

scale_free_shape_normalised_to_unit_pass.centre_fraction_definition: per pass, sum((A-B)^2 for |t| <= 15) / sum((A-B)^2 over the pass)

left_right_mirror_asymmetry_blocked_on_p.definition: per band, per pass ratio = RMS(t in [a,b)) / RMS(t in [-b,-a)); Wilcoxon and sign tests over the 22 passes vs ratio 1.0 (mirror symmetry); no sample is treated as independent

item2_center_vs_edge_rms_ratio.definition: per pass, ratio = sqrt(mean(y^2) for |t| <= 15 min) / sqrt(mean(y^2) for |t| > 15 min); one ratio per pass, n = 22

item3_within_pass_time_shuffle_null.null_definition: within each pass the sample values are randomly permuted over the fixed, irregular time stamps; the centre-vs-edge RMS ratio is recomputed. This holds the pass's own amplitude marginal distribution and sampling fixed and tests only whether the amplitude ordering in time is structured (centre-loaded) rather than exchangeable.

A.stouffer_note: no percentile hit the 1/n_perm floor; every per-pass p-value is supported by at least one null draw exceeding the observation

item3_within_pass_time_shuffle_null.percentile_definition: 100 * fraction of the pass's own null draws strictly below the observed ratio

item5_envelope_shape_fits.profile_used: pass-averaged RMS of the pairwise difference in 20 x 2-min |t| bins over [0,40] min

A-B.degeneracy_note: A fit whose parameters sit on a supplied bound has no interior optimum and its parameter values must not be quoted. The power law in |t| is additionally non-identifiable in (t0, p): its AICc/curve fit changes with the bound offered, which is itself evidence that the outer tail is heavier than a Gaussian.
A-B.parameter_names_note: constant: [amplitude]; gaussian: [amplitude, sigma_min]; lorentzian: [amplitude, hwhm_min]; sech2: [amplitude, scale_min]; power_law_in_abs_t: [a, p] in a*(|t|+0.5)^-p; power_law_shifted_t0_bounded: [a, t0, p] in a*(1+|t|/t0)^-p with t0<=100; power_law_t0_unbounded: same form with t0 free to 1e6 (ill-conditioned, kept to expose the degeneracy toward an exponential decay); shifted_center variants add a centre offset t0

item7_verdict.question: Is the leading model's advantage concentrated in the centre, at the edges, or broadly distributed?
item7_verdict.leading_model: B (established in TRACK1: B beats A in 22/22 passes, B beats C in 22/22 passes, whole-pass RMS)

A_minus_to_B_variance_reduction.interpretation: the centre region holds only ~37.5% of the samples but absorbs ~80% of the variance removed when A is replaced by B, i.e. the A->B improvement is centre-weighted, not a broad re-scaling

left_right_mirror_check.verdict: the envelope is centre-dominant but not mirror-symmetric; the asymmetry is significant only just off centre (5-10 min band, A-B Wilcoxon p = 0.00367) and has the same sign in A-B and C-B, so it is an inner-envelope feature rather than a global tilt. It is an order of magnitude smaller than the centre-vs-edge decay.

A-C.definition: per-pass RMS(A-C) ratio: outer bin |t| in [30,40) over inner bin |t| in [0,5)

C-B.definition: per-pass RMS(C-B) ratio: outer bin |t| in [30,40) over inner bin |t| in [0,5)
